title: Flank Steak with Chimichurri

steps.text: Chop the parsley and garlic together until the pieces are rice-grain small — knife-work, not a food processor, which would bruise the herbs bitter. Tip into a bowl.
Stir in the oregano, vinegar, chili flakes, half the salt, and the olive oil. Let the chimichurri sit while you cook; the vinegar mellows and the oregano swells.
Pat the steak very dry and season both sides with the rest of the salt and the pepper. Dry steak browns; wet steak grays.

Heat the grill pan over high heat until it just smokes. Lay the steak down and leave it alone for 4-5 minutes, then flip and cook 3-4 more. Flank steak is safe at 145°F (63°C) — check the thick end on a thermometer.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Move the steak to a board and rest it 5 minutes; the juices re-settle into the meat instead of the board.
Slice the steak thin, against the grain and at a slight angle — this shortens the chew of a flank.
Spoon half the chimichurri over the slices and bring the rest to the table; in Argentina there is always more sauce than steak.

cuisine_note: Chimichurri is Argentina's everyday sauce — parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar, oil, and heat, chopped raw, never blended. The same bowl seasons the steak, bread, and whatever the grill had left.
